E1:
(1) Vending machine: a ProximityPrompt only shows when its parent gives it a world position: a BasePart, an Attachment, or a Model WITH a PrimaryPart. Its parent here is a Folder inside a Model that has no PrimaryPart, so the prompt has no position and never appears. Fix: parent the prompt to a part or an Attachment (for example a hidden anchored "PromptAnchor" part or an attachment on the front panel). Or set VendingMachine.PrimaryPart and parent the prompt to the Model directly, not to a Folder.
(2) Lever: RequiresLineOfSight defaults to true, so the engine raycasts from the camera to the prompt's position, and the glass case blocks that ray. Fix: set RequiresLineOfSight = false, or move the prompt to an Attachment outside the glass. Another option is to make the glass ignored by the check (CanQuery = false while CanCollide = false), but test that it no longer blocks.
E2:
- AlwaysOnTop = false: the tag is then depth-tested, so walls and other geometry hide it. AlwaysOnTop = true draws it over everything.
- MaxDistance = 100: the gui is not rendered beyond 100 studs from the camera. The default of 0 means infinite.
- Size in Scale, not Offset, for example UDim2.fromScale(4, 1). On a BillboardGui, Scale is measured in studs, so the tag acts like a world object and shrinks with distance. Offset is screen pixels, which is why the tags stay one size. Use TextScaled (with a UITextSizeConstraint) so the text follows the frame size.
- Optional: keep StudsOffset (for example 0, 2.5, 0) to lift it above the head. Set LightInfluence = 0 so it stays readable. DistanceLowerLimit / DistanceUpperLimit / DistanceStep only change how Offset-sized guis scale, so they are not needed once you use Scale.
E3:
With CharacterAutoLoads = false the engine never spawns characters for you, not on join and not after death. Players.RespawnTime is only used by that automatic respawn, so it does nothing now. Your server has to call LoadCharacter itself. It is named Player:LoadCharacterAsync() since the Jan 2026 Async renames; the old LoadCharacter still works.
```lua
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local RESPAWN = 3
Players.PlayerAdded:Connect(function(player)
    player.CharacterAdded:Connect(function(char)
        local hum = char:WaitForChild("Humanoid")
        hum.Died:Connect(function()
            task.wait(RESPAWN)
            if player.Parent and roundActive() then -- your round logic
                player:LoadCharacterAsync()
            end
        end)
    end)
    player:LoadCharacterAsync() -- or wait until the round starts
end)
```
Only call it from the server, and check player.Parent so you don't spawn players who have already left.
E4:
CanQuery = false takes a part out of every spatial query: Raycast, shapecasts, GetPartsInPart and so on. The ray therefore never sees the glass, no matter what RaycastParams contain. (CanQuery can only be turned off when CanCollide is false, which is your setup.) Your filter isn't the problem.
Fix: set the glass to CanQuery = true and keep CanCollide = false. Players still walk through, because CanCollide is what blocks movement, and the laser ray now hits the glass. If other raycasts (guns, camera) must ignore the glass, exclude it in their params (ExcludeInstances / FilterDescendantsInstances), or tag it and filter on the hit. Note that RaycastParams.RespectCanCollide is false by default, so non-colliding parts are hit as long as CanQuery is true.
E5:
Error 1: Instance:Clone() returns nil when the instance's Archivable is false, and it also skips non-Archivable descendants. g is nil, so g:PivotTo errors. Fix: set Goblin.Archivable = true (and check descendants). Keep the template in ServerStorage, since the server spawns them.
Error 2: Destroy() sets Parent to nil, locks the Parent property, and disconnects connections. A destroyed instance can never be parented again, which is why you get "Parent property ... is locked". Never Destroy a template you plan to reuse.
Correct pattern: clone per spawn and destroy the clone.
```lua
local template = game.ServerStorage.Enemies.Goblin -- Archivable = true
local function spawnGoblin(cf)
    local g = template:Clone()
    assert(g, "Goblin not archivable")
    g:PivotTo(cf)
    g.Parent = workspace
    g.Humanoid.Died:Once(function()
        task.delay(3, function() g:Destroy() end)
    end)
    return g
end
```
If clone cost matters, pool: reset instances and park them (Parent = nil or a storage folder) instead of destroying them.

```lua
local SIZE = Vector3.new(6, 5, 6)
local DAMAGE = 20
local function swing(attacker: Model)
    local root = attacker:FindFirstChild("HumanoidRootPart")
    if not root then return end
    local boxCF = root.CFrame * CFrame.new(0, 0, -3) -- 3 studs in front
    local params = OverlapParams.new()
    params.FilterType = Enum.RaycastFilterType.Exclude
    params.FilterDescendantsInstances = {attacker} -- or params.ExcludeInstances = {attacker}
    local hitThisSwing = {}
    for _, part in workspace:GetPartBoundsInBox(boxCF, SIZE, params) do
        local model = part:FindFirstAncestorOfClass("Model")
        local hum = model and model:FindFirstChildOfClass("Humanoid")
        if hum and hum.Health > 0 and not hitThisSwing[hum] then
            hitThisSwing[hum] = true
            hum:TakeDamage(DAMAGE)
        end
    end
end
```
Accuracy caveat: GetPartBoundsInBox tests the box against each part's bounding box, not its real geometry, so rotated or mesh parts near the edges can count as hits. For exact shape tests use GetPartsInPart with a box part, which is costlier. Parts with CanQuery = false are never found. Also, the server sees other players' positions with some latency, so hits are only as accurate as the server's view.

E11:
Both fit MemoryStoreService (fast, cross-server, temporary).
- 1v1 queue: a MemoryStoreQueue. Use AddAsync to enqueue {userId, jobId}. A matchmaker calls ReadAsync(2, ..., invisibilityTimeout), pairs the players, reserves a server (TeleportService:ReserveServer and TeleportAsync), then RemoveAsync with the read id. If it crashes, the items reappear after the invisibility timeout. For skill or region buckets, use a MemoryStoreSortedMap keyed by player, with a sort key such as rating, or one queue per bucket.
- Top 100 this hour: a MemoryStoreSortedMap named per hour (for example "Scores_" .. os.date("!%Y%m%d%H")). Use key = userId, sortKey = score, and UpdateAsync to keep each player's max. Set expiration to about 3600 s plus a margin, and read with GetRangeAsync(Descending, ...) in pages. Cache the result per server and refresh every ~30-60 s instead of every server reading constantly. For all-time boards use an OrderedDataStore.
Limits:
- Memory quota: 64 KB + 1.2 KB per user.
- Requests: 1,000 + 120 x CCU per minute, experience-wide. GetRangeAsync costs 1 unit per item returned.
- Keys max 128 chars, values max 32 KB.
- Expiration is required, max 45 days (3,888,000 s).
- Sorted map: max 1M items. One map is one partition (throughput cap), so shard hot maps.
- Data is not durable, so persist anything that matters to DataStores.
E12:
Per-server budget (standard stores, per minute): Get/Set/Update/Remove each 60 + 40 x players, which is 60 + 40 x 40 = 1,660 at 40 players. List is 5 + 2 x players. UpdateAsync counts as one read plus one write.
Experience-wide (shared by all servers and Open Cloud, base raised 2026-07-29): read 300 + 40 x CCU, write 300 + 20 x CCU per minute.
Your load: 40 players autosaving every 60 s is about 40 UpdateAsync per minute, plus saves on leave, so it is well under budget. Bursts such as BindToClose saving 40 players at once must still fit. Requests over budget queue (max 30 per queue), then fail with errors 301-306.
Per key:
- Write throughput 4 MB/min, read 25 MB/min, rounded up per KB.
- Value max 4,194,304 characters, serialized JSON.
- Key, store and scope names max 50 chars.
- Don't write the same key in quick succession. The old "6 s between writes" is now a rule of thumb, so coalesce: skip the autosave if a save ran in the last few seconds, and don't double-save on leave plus BindToClose.
Practice:
- pcall every call and retry with backoff.
- Check DataStoreService:GetRequestBudgetForRequestType before bulk work.
- Use session locking or a version in UpdateAsync to avoid cross-server overwrites.

E14:
- External call: the bot calls the Open Cloud Messaging API. Current form: POST https://apis.roblox.com/cloud/v2/universes/{universeId}:publishMessage with JSON {"topic": "Announcements", "message": "<text or small JSON>"}. The legacy form is POST https://apis.roblox.com/messaging-service/v1/universes/{universeId}/topics/{topic} with {"message": ...}.
- Credentials: an Open Cloud API key from the Creator Dashboard, granted the messaging-service publish permission for that experience only, ideally IP-restricted to your bot's server, with an expiry. Send it in the x-api-key header. Keep it in the bot's env/secret store and never in game code or Discord. Only allowlisted Discord roles should trigger it.
- In-game: each server calls pcall(MessagingService.SubscribeAsync, MessagingService, "Announcements", function(msg) ... end) at startup. msg.Data is the payload and msg.Sent is the timestamp. The server validates and sanitises it, then shows it to players with a RemoteEvent:FireAllClients(text) to a UI banner. Optionally store the latest announcement elsewhere (DataStore or MemoryStore) so servers that start later can show it.
- Limits: message max 1 kB. Delivery is best-effort (usually about 1-2 s) with no guarantee. There are per-topic receive and per-server send/subscribe rate limits, so keep to one topic and few messages.
E15:
- Half-built building: by default (Nonatomic) parts stream individually. Set the model's ModelStreamingMode = Atomic so the model and all its descendants stream in and out together. The client waits for the model itself (WaitForChild with a timeout, or CollectionService tag-added signals), then sets it up. Before showing an area (teleports, cutscenes) the server can call player:RequestStreamAroundAsync(position, timeout).
- Always-present scoreboard: ModelStreamingMode = Persistent, which is sent to every client after join and never streamed out. Use PersistentPerPlayer + Model:AddPersistentPlayer(player) if only some players need it. Set these in Studio or from server Scripts, not LocalScripts. Clients should still WaitForChild, because persistent models arrive shortly after join (workspace.PersistentLoaded fires when they are all in).
Trade-offs:
- Atomic: the whole model is all-or-nothing, so a huge atomic model arrives later and costs more memory while loaded. It still streams out when far away.
- Persistent: always uses memory and bandwidth on every client and defeats streaming, so keep it to small, essential models.
- Write client code that tolerates parts appearing and disappearing anyway.
- Consider StreamOutBehavior = Opportunistic, ModelStreamingBehavior = Improved, and a tuned StreamingMinRadius/TargetRadius.
E16:
- Aim direction at 30 Hz: switch to UnreliableRemoteEvent. Only the latest value matters, and a dropped or late packet is replaced 33 ms later. A reliable remote resends and holds later packets back, which adds lag spikes and bandwidth under packet loss.
- Hit reports: keep a reliable RemoteEvent. A hit changes game state (damage, kills) and must arrive exactly once and in order. The server must still validate it (fire rate, ammo, distance, line of sight, timing) and never trust client damage.
Unreliable limits:
- Payloads over about 1,000 bytes (encoded) are dropped. Keep them tiny, for example a Vector3 or a packed buffer.
- No ordering and no delivery guarantee. Add a sequence number if order matters.
- Messages over the per-client rate budget are dropped, not delayed.
- If no handler is connected yet, messages are discarded, not queued.
- Rate-limit and sanity-check on the server too: a unit vector, max rate per player.
E17:
```lua
local SIZE = 14 -- u16 (2) + 3 x f32 (12)

local function pack(id: number, pos: Vector3): buffer
    local b = buffer.create(SIZE)
    buffer.writeu16(b, 0, id)
    buffer.writef32(b, 2, pos.X)
    buffer.writef32(b, 6, pos.Y)
    buffer.writef32(b, 10, pos.Z)
    return b
end

local function unpack(b: any): (number?, Vector3?)
    if typeof(b) ~= "buffer" or buffer.len(b) ~= SIZE then return nil end
    return buffer.readu16(b, 0),
        Vector3.new(buffer.readf32(b, 2), buffer.readf32(b, 6), buffer.readf32(b, 10))
end

-- server
ProjectileUpdate:FireAllClients(pack(id, part.Position))
-- client
ProjectileUpdate.OnClientEvent:Connect(function(b)
    local id, pos = unpack(b)
    if id then --[[ apply ]] end
end)
```
Rules:
- Offsets are zero-based byte offsets.
- Buffers are fixed-size (buffer.create(n)), and any read or write past the end throws an out-of-bounds error, so check len before reading untrusted data.
- Data is little-endian.
- Integer writes take value modulo 2^bits (writeu16 wraps outside 0-65535).
- f32 loses precision versus Luau's f64 numbers.
- Buffers replicate through remotes as one value. The encoded size must stay under the ~1,000-byte unreliable limit (14 bytes is fine).
E18:
Network ownership: every unanchored assembly is simulated either by the server or by one client, the network owner. By default the engine assigns ownership automatically, usually to the nearest player, and can hand it back and forth. When a player sits in the VehicleSeat, the seat gives that driver ownership, but if ownership flips (auto-reassignment, a passenger nearer, the server reclaiming it), the driver's inputs and the owner's simulation fight, and that is the stutter and lag.
Server fix: on Seat:GetPropertyChangedSignal("Occupant"), call SetNetworkOwner on a part of the cart assembly (welded parts share one assembly):
```lua
seat:GetPropertyChangedSignal("Occupant"):Connect(function()
    local hum = seat.Occupant
    local plr = hum and Players:GetPlayerFromCharacter(hum.Parent)
    seat:SetNetworkOwner(plr) -- nil = server when empty
end)
```
Only the server can call it, and only on unanchored parts. Check CanSetNetworkOwnership() first, and don't call SetNetworkOwnershipAuto afterwards.
Kill brick: the client that owns the cart simulates it, so the server only sees the replicated positions. Touched events for cart parts are late, jittery and can be spoofed by an exploiter. Your kill brick also reacts to any part, including the cart's own. Have the brick only act on hits whose parent is a character (Players:GetPlayerFromCharacter, Humanoid), debounce per player, and treat client-owned physics as untrusted. For important checks, do server-side spatial queries or sanity checks.

E20:
The new properties are RaycastParams.ExcludeInstances and RaycastParams.IncludeInstances, and the same pair on OverlapParams. They supersede FilterDescendantsInstances + FilterType, which still work.
Behavior:
- You can set both at once, which the old single list plus mode could not do.
- Exclusion wins over inclusion.
- IncludeInstances = nil (the default) means no include restriction (everything); {} means nothing can be hit.
- Like the old list, each entry covers its descendants.
- Reassign the arrays; don't mutate them in place. Build params once per purpose and reuse them.
```lua
local params = RaycastParams.new()
params.IncludeInstances = {workspace.Map}
params.ExcludeInstances = {workspace.Map.Glass}
local result = workspace:Raycast(origin, direction, params)
```
With the old API you would need FilterType = Include on {Map}, then a manual re-cast whenever you hit Glass. CanQuery = false parts are still never hit.

What the vault confirms (Roblox docs):
- Signature: MarketplaceService:BindReceiptHandler(receiptType: Enum.ReceiptType, handler, filter?), which returns an RBXScriptConnection you can Disconnect.
- Enum.ReceiptType values: DeveloperProduct, RobuxTransferSender, RobuxTransferReceiver.
- The handler gets the receipt info table (PurchaseId, PlayerId, ProductId, ...) and must return Enum.ReceiptDecision.Processed only after the grant has been saved, or NotProcessedYet so Roblox retries later. Errors or yields that never return count as not processed.

```lua
local COINS_100 = 1234567
local conn = MPS:BindReceiptHandler(Enum.ReceiptType.DeveloperProduct, function(info)
    if info.ProductId ~= COINS_100 then return Enum.ReceiptDecision.NotProcessedYet end
    local ok = grantCoinsIdempotent(info.PlayerId, info.PurchaseId, 100) -- DataStore UpdateAsync keyed on PurchaseId
    return ok and Enum.ReceiptDecision.Processed or Enum.ReceiptDecision.NotProcessedYet
end)
```
Unverified in the vault: the exact filter format, how several handlers matching the same product are resolved, and whether a DeveloperProduct handler can coexist with ProcessReceipt. Don't let both handle the same products. The safe default is one system per product type, with idempotent grants keyed on PurchaseId.
E24:
Luau added math.lerp and math.map in 2025, along with float helpers (math.isnan, math.isinf, math.isfinite). Constants such as math.tau followed later.
- math.lerp(a: number, b: number, t: number): number returns a + (b - a) * t, and is exact at t = 0 and t = 1. It does not clamp t.
- math.map(x: number, inMin: number, inMax: number, outMin: number, outMax: number): number remaps x linearly from [inMin, inMax] to [outMin, outMax]. It does not clamp.
Clamp with math.clamp if you don't want extrapolation. They are faster and clearer than hand-written versions. Older helpers still in the library: math.clamp, math.sign, math.round, math.noise.
